alt: Paper 2 Texts, 50% of 3247, has three parts: Part 1 Unseen Passage (20 marks, one passage-based question), Part 2 Poetry (15 marks, one of two essay questions on ten ghazals and three nazms) and Part 3 Prose (15 marks, one of two essay questions on eight articles). All test AO3 Literature.
caption: An unseen extract for 20 marks, then one poetry and one prose essay for 15 each.

after: ## The set texts at a glance
alt: Part 2 Poetry: ten ghazals by Khwaja Haider Ali Aatish, Parveen Shakir, Momin Khan Momin, Allama Iqbal and Ahmed Faraz, and three nazms by Hali (Musadas Hali, 17 stanzas), Syed Zameer Jafree (Admee) and Mirza Mahmood Sarhadi (Qitaat). Part 3 Prose: eight articles, including two of Ghalib's letters.
caption: Know each prescribed text in depth, with quotations ready.

alt: Four qualities rewarded in increasing depth: a personal, informed response; understanding beyond the literal; explicit engagement with the writer's craft (word choice, imagery, structure, tone); and close, well-selected reference to the text. The top levels need sustained, perceptive engagement with craft.
caption: Accurate comprehension is not enough: the top levels reward how the writer works.

alt: Part 1 needs a skill: practise unseen Urdu poetry and prose, identifying word choice, imagery and structure. Parts 2 and 3 need close knowledge of the set texts with quotations, and enough coverage that both question choices remain open.
caption: Practise unseen analysis; memorise set texts with quotations.

alt: A strong poetry answer identifies specific lines (sher), explains the imagery or word choice in them, and connects that language to the emotion or theme in the question. A weak answer summarises the poem's subject without close reference.
caption: Quote, explain the language, then tie it to the question.

alt: The guide's revision targets: know at least six of the ten prescribed ghazals, two of the three nazms and five of the eight prose articles in close textual detail, and time each part so Part 1 does not crowd out the essays.
caption: Enough depth across the list to keep both questions open.
